back: The account showing how the profit of a partnership is divided: salaries, interest on capital less interest on drawings, then the residual in the ratio.
Profit + interest on drawings - salaries - interest on capital = residual profit shared in the ratio.
Capital accounts stay constant; salaries, interest, profit shares and drawings go through current accounts.
No current accounts; all entries go through the capital accounts, so the balances change every year.
An expense of the business in the statement of profit or loss, not an appropriation.

front: Debit balance on a current account
back: The partner has overdrawn; it is deducted in the partners' funds.
To reward partners who invest more capital and bear more risk before the remainder is shared in the ratio.
To reward a partner who works full time or contributes more effort than the ratio would reflect.
If salaries and interest exceed the profit, the deficit is shared in the profit-sharing ratio.
